title: Rama
hook: an empty throne, and a pair of sandals keeping it
tomorrow: Ravana's own brother walks into Rama's camp. what does Rama do?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rama at the shore: Vishnu come as a human to teach humans, a god who asked the ocean first. Today, his brother, and two sandals.

A family might keep a seat empty at the table while someone's away. On the throne of Ayodhya there's no king. There's a pair of wooden sandals. The man who could sit there lives outside the city in bark clothes, and every decision he makes, he makes in the sandals' name. His name is Bharata, and the sandals are his brother's.
screen: `A SEAT KEPT EMPTY.` → `SANDALS ON THE THRONE.` → `BHARATA RULES IN THEIR NAME.`

segments.voice: Bharata was given the kingdom by a promise his father made to Bharata's mother, the same promise that sent Rama into the forest. He wants none of it. In Valmiki's Ramayana he goes after Rama and begs him to come home. Rama won't; his father's word stands. So Bharata asks for his sandals, sets them on the throne, and rules as their servant. In the Bhagavata, when Rama finally returns, Bharata comes out carrying the sandals on his head and sets them at his brother's feet. Now the week, in one breath. Vamana's third stride landed on a bowed head. Two bowls were swapped, and a sage's son carried an axe. One son obeyed a terrible order, two refused, and the argument stays open. A father said: our strength is forgiveness. The axe stepped aside for the bow and kept teaching. A god waited at a shore. And here, a brother held a throne for someone else. Different forms, different books, and in each, someone lets go of what they could have kept.
screen: `THE THRONE HE DIDN'T WANT.` · `SANDALS IN THE KING'S SEAT.` · `CARRIED HOME ON HIS HEAD.` · `LETTING GO OF WHAT YOU COULD KEEP.`

segments.voice: Feel your feet on the floor, the soles resting, your weight settling down through them. Stay with that contact for the sit, steady and unhurried, as if someone else were keeping your place for you while you rest.
Rama: the prince whose brother set his sandals on the throne and ruled in their name until he came home.
Your line: Rama. His brother kept the throne for him with a pair of sandals. A week ends here.

chat.meaning: Bharata set Rama's sandals on the throne and kept his place until he came home. Keeping someone's place is a way of loving them.
